title: Central German Study for Immunotherapy in Thoracic Surgery
summary:
Neoadjuvant treatment regimens in the therapy of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) are being used more and more frequently in clinical practice and present clinicians with ever new challenges. In particular, neoadjuvant therapy with immune checkpoint inhibitors (pembrolizumab, nivolumab, etc.) in combination with established chemotherapeutic agents sometimes requires a rethinking and questioning of established treatment strategies. While these drugs were initially only used in clinical trials (e.g. CheckMate 816, Keynote-671, etc.), since the approval of various preparations for the treatment of operable NSCLC, we are increasingly treating neoadjuvantly pretreated patients who present us with problems attributable to neoadjuvant treatment with immune checkpoint inhibitors. 

There is now a need for an open discussion from a thoracic surgery perspective based on real-world evidence. A multicentre study would be ideal for this purpose. It would include neoadjuvant-treated patients who underwent surgery for NSCLC.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of bronchus and lung

interventions.name: Patients who underwent surgery following neoadjuvant immunochemotherapy and surgery for NSCLC

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Preoperative immunotherapy prior to resection of NSCLC
Surgery after 31 December 2022
Exclusion criteria:
Patients without prior neoadjuvant treatment with an immune checkpoint inhibitor in their personal medical history
Surgery for palliative purposes (e.g. debulking, tumour haemorrhage, etc.)
